title: Mirik in comfort: lake, tea and Gopaldhara
start: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport
end: NJP railway station or Bagdogra airport

Lake-view rooms, 3 nights with breakfast and dinner

meta_description: Mirik in comfort, 3 nights from ₹18,500: lake-view rooms, Tingling and Sourenee, Bokar Monastery, a Gopaldhara high-tea morning and a private car.
summary: Three relaxed nights in a lake-view room at Mirik with a private car. Stop at Tingling and Sourenee on the way up, sit in on prayers at Bokar Monastery, drive up to the high tea of Gopaldhara for a misty morning and a tasting, and walk the orange orchards in season. From about ₹18,500 per person.
intro: Mirik rewards a slow stay. This trip gives you three nights in one comfortable room with a view of the lake, so you can walk at dawn, nap after lunch and watch the light change in the evening without packing a bag.

A private car opens up the valley: the famous tea viewpoints on the climb from Dudhia, the monastery hill, and a morning on the high slopes of Gopaldhara, at up to 2,100 m one of the highest tea gardens in Darjeeling. Good for couples and for parents travelling with grown-up children.
highlights: A lake-view room for three nights

days.title: NJP to Mirik via Tingling
days.drive: ≈ 52 km · 2.5–3 h by private car with stops
days.text: Your car meets you at NJP or Bagdogra and drives via Matigara to Dudhia on the Balason. Climb through the tea gardens to Tingling viewpoint and Sourenee, stopping for photographs and a cup of tea. Check into a lake-view room in Mirik for lunch and spend the evening on a slow walk across the footbridge.

days.title: Lake, Bokar and Rameetay Dara
days.text: Walk round Sumendu Lake at dawn. After breakfast, drive up to Bokar Monastery for morning prayers, then on to Rameetay Dara. In the afternoon, walk out along an estate road into the tea and orange slopes with a local guide, or take a rowing boat on the lake.

days.title: Gopaldhara high tea morning
days.drive: ≈ 30–45 min each way by private car
days.text: Drive up early to the high slopes of Gopaldhara, where tea grows at 1,700–2,100 m. On clear winter mornings the Mirik valley lies under mist below you. Walk a stretch of estate road where access is open. Back in Mirik, taste a first and second flush from Gopaldhara or another Mirik garden in a good tea shop and compare them. Spend the afternoon at leisure.

days.title: Mirik to NJP
days.text: After breakfast and a last look at the lake, drive down to NJP or Bagdogra, arriving by early afternoon. Stop at Dudhia if you want to see the Balason river.

includes: Private car with driver for transfers and sightseeing

Local guides and tastings where listed
excludes: Flights and trains to NJP or Bagdogra
save_money: Travel midweek, when lake-view rooms cost less.
Keep the car only for transfer days and the Gopaldhara morning; walk the rest.
Buy tea after tasting, and only what you will drink within a year.
good_to_know: Gopaldhara factory visits are not routine; the trip does not depend on one.
Mirik lake gets crowded from late morning on weekends.
Gopaldhara is several degrees colder than Mirik; carry a warm layer.

faqs.a: Yes. ₹18,500 is per person on twin sharing for Indian nationals, from NJP or Bagdogra and back, as an indicative 2025–26 figure. Solo travellers pay more for rooms and cars; groups of four sharing a car pay less. We round to the nearest ₹500.

faqs.q: Can we start from Bagdogra airport instead of NJP?
faqs.a: Yes. Bagdogra is about 30 minutes from Siliguri and a little further from NJP. Shared autos and taxis link the airport to the Siliguri jeep stands. With a reserved car, the fare from Bagdogra is about the same as from NJP.

faqs.q: Can we change the number of nights?
faqs.a: Yes. Add a night where you want more time, usually in the village stops, or drop one on a tight schedule. Keep at least two nights in any place where you want a clear dawn view, since weather can spoil one morning.

faqs.q: Which hotel do you use in Mirik for this trip?
faqs.a: We suggest a lake-view room in one of Krishnanagar's better family hotels, or the GTA's Swiss Cottages on the hill above the lake for space and quiet. Prices vary by season; compare current rates before booking.

faqs.q: Can we visit the Gopaldhara factory?
faqs.a: Factory visits are not routine and depend on the estate. We plan the morning around the high garden roads, the view and a tasting in Mirik, so the trip works without a factory visit. Ask locally; sometimes access is possible.

faqs.q: Is this trip good for a honeymoon?
faqs.a: Yes. One comfortable room for three nights, a private car, quiet mornings by the lake and a misty tea-garden dawn make it a calm, romantic trip at a moderate cost. Ask for a room with a lake view and a heater in winter.

Yes. On day 4, instead of going down to NJP, drive about 2 hours over the ridge via Sukhia Pokhari to Darjeeling and stay two nights there. The car fare from Mirik to Darjeeling is about ₹2,500–3,200.

faqs.q: What is the best time for this trip?
faqs.a: November and December for clear mornings and oranges; March to May for tea and spring. The Gopaldhara mist-and-sunrise effect is best on clear winter mornings.

faqs.q: Is a private car really needed in Mirik?
faqs.a: Not for the town itself, which is small. It is useful for the viewpoint stops on the way up, the monastery hill and the dawn drive to Gopaldhara. If you prefer, use the car only on those days.
